adopt-adapt.notes: r16 release. The excludes are exactly scripts/package.py private_files() on the release tree; release.json is regenerated by the skill's own manifest(). Version 3.0.0-grok-draft.r16 ships as released: tests/test_r16.py pins SKILL.md, package.py VERSION and the CHANGES.md heading to it, so no portfolio suffix is applied. The license line is unchanged: it matches NOTICE.md.

CHANGES.md.reason: The canonical changelog carries private project names, machine paths and internal review notes (the file the package manifest requires). The public edition is a condensed changelog of the r16 line that keeps the heading and phrases the skill's tests pin.

evals/trigger-evals.json.reason: Routing cases that name private projects, machine paths and a real directory are rewritten against the public profiles (generic, coding-workflow, frankenmine, westack, self); each case keeps its intent and expected routing logic. The skill's own PUBLIC_OVERLAYS declares this file as one the public build must replace.

description.text: Evaluate pasted repos, papers, products, docs, posts, datasets or agent skills for mechanisms a user-named recipient (a project, a coding workflow, Frankenmine, westack, or this skill itself) should ADOPT, ADAPT, or DISCARD, with evidence-backed transfer plans. Use for "adopt-adapt", "adopt or adapt these", "should this project use this", "mine these links", "salvage anything from this". Not for implementing an already-chosen tool, ordinary code review, product how-to, or merely wiring recipient paths. A new product built from several sources belongs to frankenmine; recovering how one opaque product, binary or app works belongs to reverse-engineer-anything.
description.reason: Drops the private project list from the trigger description.

frankenmine.notes: Version 0.2.0 ships as released; the build applies no portfolio suffix. evidence/ is omitted except evidence/synthetic-run/, which tests/v0_2_tests.py loads and which is clean: the other receipts and logs (results.json, CONTINUATION_STARTER.json, development-trial/) carry machine paths and private project names, so they are excluded rather than rewritten, as are the review records beside them. Everything else is byte-identical to the release commit apart from the overlays.

BUILD_REPORT.md.reason: Points the omitted evidence/ receipts and the private install-sync instruction at a public-edition note. Keeps the four old-name release-note mentions its rename guard counts.

README.md.reason: Replaces links to the omitted evidence/ reviews with a statement that they are omitted, and notes that the design specification is a redacted public copy.

evals/LIVE_AGENT_PROTOCOL.md.reason: The exploratory trial it cites under evidence/development-trial/ is omitted.

evals/evals.json.reason: Eval 4 names private projects and one project's extraction rule; the same routing case is kept with a generic recipient.

references/research.md.reason: The canonical text says research/ is byte-for-byte; the public design specification is redacted.

research/FRANKENMINE_DESIGN_SPEC.md.reason: Hash-pinned research note: citations to a private repository replaced with links to this collection, plus a distribution note. The four old-name mentions its rename guard counts are untouched. Published sha256 is pinned in the scripts/package.py overlay.

research/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.json.reason: Drops a private Library file ID and records the redacted specification's published bytes next to the supplied hash. Base is the CRLF bytes of the release commit; the overlay keeps CRLF.

scripts/package.py.reason: Explicit expected-hash change for the redacted FRANKENMINE_DESIGN_SPEC.md; no other line changes.

tests/westack_rename_tests.py.reason: Its allowlist rows name four receipts and review records under evidence/ that this edition omits (machine paths, private project names), so the rows are removed and the planted-receipt control targets BUILD_REPORT.md (4 counted mentions) instead of evidence/results.json. The scanner, every other row and every other control are unchanged.

westack.notes: Two records ship although the rest of tests/results/ does not: provenance/ARTIFACT_REVIEW.md (a dated review) and tests/results/tests-final.json (the final test receipt). Both are clean on the leak patterns, and westack's own rename guard lists both in its keep list, so an edition that omits them fails that guard. The other receipts stay excluded as machine-specific transcripts; 12 of them contain machine paths and private project names.

provenance/RIGHTS.md.reason: The collection also publishes adopt-adapt, so 'not bundled, relicensed or redistributed' becomes 'not bundled into westack or relicensed by westack'. Re-pinned to westack 0.3.1 (commit 37feb98); every other byte is the canonical file.
